symbols.name: d
symbols.role: Indexes control and treatment potential-outcome surfaces.

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: \(S\) is the compact polygonal geographic score support.

symbols.name: Y_d
symbols.def: \(Y(d)\) is the potential outcome under arm \(d\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: \(B\) separates the two assignment sides of \(S\).

symbols.name: S_d
symbols.def: \(S_d\) is the closure of the side assigned arm \(d\), with \(S_0\cap S_1=B\).

symbols.name: J_d
symbols.def: \(J_d\) indexes the observed areal cells on side \(d\).
symbols.role: Dimension of the arm-specific information vector.

symbols.name: mu_dj
symbols.def: \(\mu_{dj}\) is the conditional law of \(X\) in observed cell \(C_{dj}\).

symbols.name: w
symbols.def: \(w\) is the known density of the target measure relative to boundary length.
symbols.role: Weights heterogeneous effects along the boundary.

symbols.name: M_d
symbols.def: \(M_d\) is the separately selected maintained Lipschitz radius for arm \(d\).

symbols.name: g_d
symbols.def: \(g_d:S\to\mathbb R\) is a generic class member for arm \(d\).
symbols.role: Bound variable in the response-surface class.

symbols.name: F_d
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_d\) is the clipped \(M_d\)-Lipschitz class defined in \(\mathrm{def:surface-class}\).

symbols.name: A_d
symbols.role: Maps a surface to observed cell means.

symbols.name: U_d
symbols.role: Sharp upper boundary mean for arm \(d\).

symbols.name: L_d
symbols.role: Sharp lower boundary mean for arm \(d\).

symbols.name: sigma
symbols.role: Residual measure in the support problem.

symbols.name: H_Md
symbols.role: Inner support cost in the endpoint dual.

symbols.name: E_d
symbols.role: Affine geometry of the moment body.

symbols.name: T_h
symbols.def: Fix one rational triangulation \(\mathcal T_0\) conforming to \(B\), all cell boundaries, and all density and boundary-weight knots. Recursively form \(\mathcal T_{k+1}\) by joining the three rational edge midpoints of every triangle of \(\mathcal T_k\), and write \(\mathcal T_h=\mathcal T_k\) when \(h=\max_{T\in\mathcal T_k}\operatorname{diam}(T)\).

symbols.name: N_h
symbols.def: \(\mathcal N_h\) is the vertex set of \(\mathcal T_h\), ordered lexicographically by its rational coordinates.
symbols.role: Common finite support for the atomic program.

symbols.name: p_djh
symbols.def: \(p_{dj,h}(x)\) is the lexicographically first element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathcal N_h\cap C_{dj}}\|x-z\|_2\).
symbols.role: Pushes each cell score law to rational mesh nodes without ambiguity.

symbols.name: p_Bh
symbols.def: \(p_{B,h}(x)\) is the lexicographically first element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathcal N_h\cap B}\|x-z\|_2\).
symbols.role: Pushes the boundary law to rational boundary nodes without ambiguity.

symbols.name: mu_djh
symbols.role: Exact pushed-forward cell weights in the atomic moment constraints.

symbols.name: nu_h
symbols.role: Exact pushed-forward weights in the atomic boundary objective.

symbols.name: v_dh
symbols.role: Decision variable of the finite atomic relaxation.

symbols.name: E_dh
symbols.space: maps feasible nodal vectors to \(\mathcal F_d\)
symbols.role: Converts every pairwise-Lipschitz nodal solution into a canonical continuous feasible surface.

symbols.name: F_dh
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_{d,h}\) contains the continuous functions affine on each triangle of \(\mathcal T_h\) that satisfy the exact range and Euclidean Lipschitz inequalities.

symbols.name: P_dh
symbols.role: Certified exactly moment-feasible lower bound on \(U_d\).

symbols.name: V_dh
symbols.def: \(V_{d,h}(m_d)\) is the maximum of \(\sum_{z\in\mathcal N_h}v_{d,h,z}\nu_h(\{z\})\) subject to \(0\le v_{d,h,z}\le1\), \(|v_{d,h,z}-v_{d,h,z'}|\le M_d\|z-z'\|_2\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathcal N_h\), and \(\left|\sum_zv_{d,h,z}\mu_{dj,h}(\{z\})-m_{dj}\right|\le M_dh\) for every \(j\in J_d\).

symbols.name: VPA
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{VPA}\) starts from conforming rational midpoint refinement, exact integration of piecewise-affine functions, relative-interior moment correction, and outward interval enclosures of Euclidean lengths and partial-transport dual objectives; its target is a terminating certified primal--dual endpoint routine.
symbols.role: Concrete handle for the open computational theorem.

symbols.name: n_dj
symbols.def: \(n_{dj}\) is fixed conditional on the sampling design.

symbols.name: mhat_dj
symbols.role: Observed sufficient statistic for confidence inversion.

symbols.name: Q_n
symbols.role: Finite-sample simultaneous region for all areal means.

symbols.name: C_n
symbols.space: compact intervals in \(\mathbb R\) or the empty set
symbols.role: Confidence set that contains the full identified interval.

symbols.name: a
symbols.role: Width normal to a rectangular boundary.

symbols.name: ell_d
symbols.role: Indexes clipping regimes in the rectangle formulas.

symbols.name: t
symbols.role: Scalar argument of the rectangle envelope.

symbols.name: eps
symbols.def: \(\epsilon\) is supplied as an exactly represented rational number.

symbols.name: G_sens
symbols.space: finite sets of score-law and smoothness specifications
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{sens}}\) is a prespecified finite collection of pairs \(\bigl((\mu_{dj})_{d,j},(M_0,M_1)\bigr)\) constructed by the protocol in \(\mathrm{def:application-sensitivity-protocol}\).
symbols.role: Prevents a sign conclusion from resting on one unreported score-law or smoothness choice.

assumptions.condition: \(S\) is a compact convex rational polygon.

standard.name: Compact semialgebraic support specialized to a rational polygon

assumptions.condition: \(B\) is a finite union of rational line segments.
For each \(d\), the interiors of \(C_{dj}\), \(j\in J_d\), are pairwise disjoint.

standard.name: Spatial-cell version of fixed aggregate categories

assumptions.condition: For each \(d\), the union of \(C_{dj}\), \(j\in J_d\), covers the observed portion of \(S_d\) up to area zero.
Every within-cell score law \(\mu_{dj}\) is known to the analyst rather than estimated from the outcome sample.

novel.justification: This maintained input is credible when administrative population registers or complete geocoded sampling frames determine within-cell location weights independently of the outcome sample; applications without such records must vary the score laws in the prespecified sensitivity grid.

assumptions.condition: Each \(\mu_{dj}\) has a rational piecewise-constant Lebesgue density on a conforming rational triangulation.

novel.justification: Rational piecewise-constant densities cover uniform-within-polygon records and histogram weights exported from administrative population rasters, while permitting exact cell integration on a rational refinement.

assumptions.condition: The density of each \(\mu_{dj}\) is bounded above and bounded away from zero on \(C_{dj}\).
\(w\) belongs to the cone of nonnegative piecewise-affine functions on \(B\).

novel.justification: Separate maintained radii allow treatment and control response surfaces to have different spatial regularity; applications select each radius from outcome-scale scientific bounds and report the full prespecified sensitivity frontier rather than treating either radius as known from boundary-RD theory.

standard.name: Compatibility with a sharp identified set

assumptions.condition: \(r_d(m_d)>0\) for each arm to which the relative-interior computational claim is applied.
Conditional on the fixed counts \(n_{dj}\), the variables \(Y_{dji}\) are mutually independent.

definitions.name: Clipped Lipschitz response class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_d=\{g_d\in C(S):0\le g_d(x)\le1\ \text{for all }x\in S,\ |g_d(x)-g_d(y)|\le M_d\|x-y\|_2\ \text{for all }x,y\in S\}\), for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\).

definitions.name: Areal moment map
definitions.construction: \(A_d:\mathcal F_d\to\mathbb R^{|J_d|}\) is given by \((A_dg_d)_j=\int_Sg_d\,d\mu_{dj}\) for every \(j\in J_d\) and \(d\in\{0,1\}\).

definitions.name: Exact-moment piecewise-affine program
definitions.construction: On the deterministic nested midpoint refinement \(\mathcal T_h\), let \(\mathcal F_{d,h}=\{q\in C(S):q|_T\text{ is affine},\ 0\le q(z)\le1\text{ for every }z\in\mathcal N_h,\ \|\nabla(q|_T)\|_2\le M_d\text{ for every }T\in\mathcal T_h\}\) and set \(P_{d,h}(m_d)=\max\{\int_Bq\,d\nu:q\in\mathcal F_{d,h},\ A_dq=m_d\}\).

definitions.name: Atomic outer program
definitions.construction:
For each \(C_{dj}\) and for \(B\), project a point to its nearest node in \(\mathcal N_h\) lying in the same set, breaking distance ties by the lexicographic order of rational node coordinates. Thus \(p_{dj,h}\) and \(p_{B,h}\) are single-valued and satisfy \(\|x-p_{dj,h}(x)\|_2\le h\) and \(\|x-p_{B,h}(x)\|_2\le h\). Set \(\mu_{dj,h}=(p_{dj,h})_\#\mu_{dj}\) and \(
u_h=(p_{B,h})_\#
u\). Define \(V_{d,h}(m_d)\) as the maximum of \(\sum_{z\in\mathcal N_h}v_{d,h,z}
u_h(\{z\})\) over \(v_{d,h}\) satisfying \(0\le v_{d,h,z}\le1\), \(|v_{d,h,z}-v_{d,h,z'}|\le M_d\|z-z'\|_2\) for every \(z,z'\in\mathcal N_h\), and the exact relaxed-moment constraints \(\left|\sum_{z\in\mathcal N_h}v_{d,h,z}\mu_{dj,h}(\{z\})-m_{dj}ight|\le M_dh\) for every \(j\in J_d\). Set \(B_{d,h}(m_d)=\min\{1,V_{d,h}(m_d)+M_dh\}\), and associate each feasible vector with the canonical extension \(E_{d,h}v_{d,h}\).

definitions.name: Application-facing score-law and smoothness sensitivity protocol
definitions.construction: Before evaluating outcomes, construct \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{sens}}\) by taking the within-cell score laws from a complete geocoded population frame when available and otherwise including uniform-cell and prespecified population-density alternatives, then crossing those laws with separate finite grids for \(M_0\) and \(M_1\) calibrated from outcome-scale scientific bounds and negative-control spatial gradients. Report \(I(m_0,m_1)\) for every element of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{sens}}\), the envelope of those intervals, and a sign certificate only when every reported interval excludes zero with the same sign.

definitions.name: Verified primal--dual algorithm handle
definitions.construction: Use conforming rational midpoint refinement, exact integration of piecewise-affine functions, relative-interior moment correction, and outward interval enclosures of Euclidean lengths and clipping-aware partial-transport dual objectives to design \(\mathsf{VPA}\) for a requested rational tolerance.

statements.statement: For every compatible \((m_0,m_1)\in K_0\times K_1\), the sharp mean-information identified set for \(\tau_B\) is \[I(m_0,m_1)=[L_1(m_1)-U_0(m_0),\ U_1(m_1)-L_0(m_0)].\] Both endpoints and every intermediate value are attained by a pair \((f_0,f_1)\in\mathcal F_0\times\mathcal F_1\), and each such pair lifts to a bounded Bernoulli potential-outcome law with the prescribed conditional means and exact observed cell means.
statements.justification: Compact moment fibers establish causal sharpness rather than a merely variational outer bound.
statements.gap: Qiu and Stoye impose Euclidean Lipschitz smoothness in equation \(2.1\), formulate their tight bounded isotropic extrapolation program in equation \(2.2\), and give a one-coordinate weakening in equation \(2.3\). Their framework informs the smoothness geometry here, but neither it nor Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu identifies a boundary functional from fixed areal integrals.
statements.consumer: A district-level child-stunting analysis can report a resolution-honest sign only if the complete mean-compatible interval excludes zero throughout the prespecified score-law and arm-specific-radius sensitivity grid.

statements.statement: For every finite signed \(\sigma\) on \(S\), \[H_{M_d}(\sigma)=\min_{\pi\in\Pi_{\le}(\sigma)}\left\{\sigma^+(S)-\pi(S\times S)+M_d\int_{S\times S}\|x-y\|_2\,d\pi(x,y)\right\},\] and the minimum is attained. After the affine transformation \(\phi=2g_d-1\) and the corresponding ground-metric rescaling, this support identity is equivalent to Piccoli and Rossi's generalized \(W_1^{1,1}\) flat-metric dual. For every \(m_d\in K_d\), \[U_d(m_d)=\inf_{\lambda_d\in\mathbb R^{|J_d|}}D_d(\lambda_d;m_d),\qquad L_d(m_d)=1-U_d(\mathbf 1-m_d).\] No condition \(\sum_{j\in J_d}\lambda_{dj}=1\) is imposed. A finite minimizing \(\lambda_d\) exists whenever \(r_d(m_d)>0\). In the one-cell unit-rectangle specialization with uniform \(\mu_{dj}\), uniform boundary \(\nu\), \(M_d=1\), and \(m_d=0\), the primal value is zero but every finite multiplier has strictly positive dual objective, so multiplier attainment fails at that boundary mean.
statements.justification: The theorem turns an infinite-dimensional clipped inverse problem into an evaluable partial-transport support cost while identifying the exact multiplier-attainment frontier needed for computation.
statements.gap: Piccoli and Rossi's Theorem 13 has no exact areal side moments. Qiu and Stoye's equations \(2.1\)--\(2.3\) inform the bounded isotropic geometry, but their boundary-to-policy extrapolation problem has no areal moment operator or unrestricted cell-moment multipliers.
statements.consumer: Certified endpoint software can use a transport flow at each multiplier and will not misdiagnose a boundary mean as a numerical optimization failure.

statements.statement: Three complete planar reductions hold. First, for one uniform cell \([0,a]\times[0,1]\) and uniform boundary law on \(\{0\}\times[0,1]\), \(U_d(m_d)=\max\{t\in[0,1]:A_{\ell_d}(t)\le m_d\}\), equivalently \[U_d(m_d)=\begin{cases}1,&m_d\ge A_{\ell_d}(1),\\ \sqrt{2\ell_dm_d},&m_d<A_{\ell_d}(1)\ \text{and }m_d\le\ell_d/2,\\ m_d+\ell_d/2,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad L_d(m_d)=1-U_d(1-m_d).\] Second, on the unit rectangle with \(M_d=1\) and horizontal density \(\rho_\star\), \[U_d(m_d)=\begin{cases}\sqrt{4m_d/3},&0\le m_d\le3/16,\\ \sqrt{3/2+4m_d}-1,&3/16\le m_d\le5/8,\\1,&5/8\le m_d\le1,\end{cases}\qquad L_d(m_d)=1-U_d(1-m_d).\] Third, on the triangle with vertices \((-1,0),(1,0),(0,1)\), split at \(x=0\), with uniform area laws and boundary density \(w(0,y)=2(1-y)\), one has \([L_d(m_d),U_d(m_d)]=[m_d-M_d/3,m_d+M_d/3]\) whenever \(0\le M_d\le3/4\) and \(2M_d/3\le m_d\le1-2M_d/3\).
statements.justification: Closed forms expose clipping transitions, density sensitivity, and nonconstant boundary weights that an abstract optimization display conceals.
statements.gap: The closest boundary papers provide estimators or a coordinate projection radius, while the flat-metric literature does not invert exact areal means into these endpoint laws.
statements.consumer: The formulas give immediate fixed-resolution sign and informativeness checks before any general-purpose numerical solve.

statements.statement: For the fixed nested midpoint refinement and the lexicographically tie-broken projections, \(\|x-p_{dj,h}(x)\|_2\le h\) on every \(C_{dj}\) and \(\|x-p_{B,h}(x)\|_2\le h\) on \(B\). Consequently every \(g_d\in\mathcal F_d\) yields a feasible nodal vector \(v_{d,h,z}=g_d(z)\), its cell and boundary pushforward errors are at most \(M_dh\), and \(U_d(m_d)\le B_{d,h}(m_d)\) for every \(m_d\in K_d\). For every compatible mean, \(B_{d,h}(m_d)\to U_d(m_d)\) as \(h\downarrow0\). For every atomic optimizer \(v_{d,h}\), the canonical extension satisfies \[\left\|A_d(E_{d,h}v_{d,h})-m_d\right\|_2\le2M_dh\sqrt{|J_d|},\qquad \left|\int_BE_{d,h}v_{d,h}\,d\nu-\sum_{z\in\mathcal N_h}v_{d,h,z}\nu_h(\{z\})\right|\le M_dh.\] If \(r_d(m_d)>0\), relative-interior endpoint stability gives \(U_d(A_dE_{d,h}v_{d,h})\le U_d(m_d)+\|A_dE_{d,h}v_{d,h}-m_d\|_2/r_d(m_d)\); adding the boundary projection error and the \(M_dh\) correction in \(B_{d,h}\) yields exactly \[0\le B_{d,h}(m_d)-U_d(m_d)\le2M_dh\left(1+\frac{\sqrt{|J_d|}}{r_d(m_d)}\right).\] The exact-moment piecewise-affine fiber is then nonempty for all sufficiently small \(h\), \(P_{d,h}(m_d)\le U_d(m_d)\), and \[0\le U_d(m_d)-P_{d,h}(m_d)\le\varepsilon_{d,h}\left(1+\frac{\sqrt{|J_d|}}{r_d(m_d)}\right),\qquad \varepsilon_{d,h}=O(\sqrt h).\] The reflected programs give the corresponding lower-endpoint bounds and shrinking a posteriori effect-set gaps when certified finite-program optimization errors vanish.
statements.justification: The result separates universal value-side approximation from exact primal recovery and quantifies precisely where relative-interior slack repairs continuous moments.
statements.gap: Mula and Nouy prove moment-hierarchy convergence, and Baldi and Mourrain quantify pseudo-moment approximation, but neither supplies this exact response-surface moment correction or its clipping-preserving endpoint gap.
statements.consumer: A practitioner receives a monotonically valid outer interval at every compatible mean and a convergent exact-feasibility inner certificate away from exposed faces.

statements.statement: For rational polygonal input, rational piecewise-constant cell densities, rational piecewise-affine boundary weights, rational \(M_d\), rational \(m_d\) with \(r_d(m_d)>0\), and rational \(\epsilon>0\), can \(\mathsf{VPA}\) be completed and proved to terminate with an exactly moment-feasible continuous piecewise-affine primal surface and rational outward lower and upper enclosures of both arm endpoints whose gaps are at most \(\epsilon\)? The required certificate must verify exact continuous cell integrals, every clipping inequality, every Euclidean gradient inequality, and the continuous dual remainder rather than accept floating residuals.
statements.justification: This is the nonroutine bridge from asymptotic mathematical convergence to a terminating auditable endpoint certificate.
statements.gap: Mula and Nouy stop at convergent moments and approximate post-processing; Baldi and Mourrain's exact extraction requires flat truncation and zero-dimensional geometry, which need not hold for Lipschitz optimizer faces.
statements.consumer: A successful routine would turn a Dell-style sign conclusion into a reproducible certificate whose validity does not depend on solver tolerances.

statements.statement: Under conditional cell-sample independence, \[\inf\Pr\{I(m_0,m_1)\subseteq C_n\}\ge1-\gamma,\] where the infimum ranges over all maintained bounded cell-outcome laws with the fixed score laws and compatible means. Whenever \(Q_n\cap(K_0\times K_1)\neq\varnothing\), \(C_n\) is an attained compact interval equal to the effect image of all response-surface pairs whose joint moment vector lies in \(Q_n\). If \(r_d(m_d)>0\) for both arms and \(\min_{d,j}n_{dj}\to\infty\), then the Hausdorff distance between \(C_n\) and \(I(m_0,m_1)\) converges to zero in probability.
statements.justification: The theorem covers both endpoints and every value in the sharp set without differentiating a potentially nonsmooth endpoint map.
statements.gap: Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer give asymptotic criterion inversion, while Qiu and Stoye use an exact-normal approximation and Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu infer a point-valued boundary curve from unit-level data.
statements.consumer: A sign certificate remains valid after simultaneous sampling uncertainty in every district-level stunting mean is propagated through identification.

statements.statement: The kernel obeys three known-case reductions. If \(M_d=0\), compatibility forces every coordinate of \(m_d\) to equal a common constant and \(L_d(m_d)=U_d(m_d)\) equals that constant. In the one-cell uniform rectangle with \(a=M_d=1\) and \(m_d=1/2\), each arm interval is \([0,1]\), so equal arm means give \(I(m_0,m_1)=[-1,1]\). If \(m_1=7/8\) and \(m_0=1/32\) in that same geometry, then \(I(m_0,m_1)=[1/4,1]\).
statements.justification: The reductions check the zero-smoothness limit, the logically vacuous fixed-resolution case, and a nonvacuous sign-identifying case.
statements.gap: These are required internal reductions rather than novelty claims; no closest-paper improvement is asserted.
statements.consumer: They serve as analytic regression tests for any implementation of the general endpoint program.

sampling_model.design: Fixed finitely many areal cells with maintained known within-cell score laws and fixed cell counts for inference.
sampling_model.units: Within each observed cell, \(Y_{dji}\in[0,1]\) are mutually independent conditional on the counts and satisfy \(\mathbb E[Y_{dji}]=m_{dj}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Sharp geographic assignment gives arm \(d\) on side \(S_d\); assignment on \(B\) is irrelevant because every cell score law gives \(B\) zero mass.
sampling_model.overlap: No cross-boundary overlap is required; identification comes from known assignment, exact areal means, clipping, and arm-specific Lipschitz restrictions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only cell means are sampled. The score laws are maintained as known from an outcome-independent geocoded frame, and the two Lipschitz radii are maintained separately; the application reports the complete prespecified score-law and radius sensitivity grid from \(\mathrm{def:application-sensitivity-protocol}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their equation \(2.1\) imposes the Euclidean Lipschitz restriction, equation \(2.2\) is the tight bounded isotropic boundary-to-policy program, and equation \(2.3\) is explicitly a one-coordinate weakening.
Their Theorem 13 equates generalized unequal-mass \(W_1\) with the bounded-Lipschitz flat metric.
Their hierarchy theorem gives monotone convergence of transport relaxation values and subsequential convergence of moments.
Their flat-truncation theorem characterizes finite exact pseudo-moment recovery through zero-dimensional minimizer geometry under finite convergence.
Their effective Positivstellensatz yields quantitative approximation of truncated pseudo-moments by genuine moments.
Their Theorems 1 and 2 provide rates and Gaussian inference for aggregated effects formed from unit-level observations near a shrinking boundary region.
Their location-based theorems provide pointwise and uniform inference for boundary effect curves estimated from individual bivariate scores.
Her propositions characterize aggregate-data bounds with finite-support covariates and polyhedral restrictions.
They establish asymptotic confidence regions for criterion-defined identified sets.

tldr: Fixed geographic cells reveal integrals of latent response surfaces, not their boundary traces. Under maintained known polygonal score laws, bounded outcomes, and separately calibrated arm-specific isotropic Lipschitz restrictions, the weighted boundary effect has an attained sharp interval whose support values equal clipping-aware partial-transport costs inside an unrestricted exact-moment multiplier dual. Closed-form rectangle, nonuniform-density, and weighted-triangle laws expose when fixed resolution is vacuous, informative, or sign identifying. Deterministically projected atomic outer programs converge with an explicit correction, exact-moment piecewise-affine inner programs converge on the relative interior with quantitative gaps, and simultaneous bounded-mean box inversion covers the whole identified interval in finite samples. The application reports a prespecified score-law and radius sensitivity frontier, while a terminating exact-arithmetic primal reconstruction and dual-enclosure routine remains the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Boundary-discontinuity methods observe units approaching the assignment boundary, whereas many historical and administrative applications expose only fixed areal means. Existing tight smoothness programs do not invert these area integrals, and existing unequal-mass transport or moment hierarchies do not combine clipping, exact cell moments, causal endpoint lifting, and finite stopping certificates.
project_justification.niche: The observation operator is finite-dimensional but the target is singular with respect to every cell law. This creates a clipped moment-fiber geometry in which primal extrema exist universally, outer multipliers can diverge on exposed faces, and exact continuous primal recovery becomes possible locally only through relative-interior slack.
project_justification.fill: The project characterizes the exact causal set and its transport dual, proves the multiplier-attainment frontier and analytic planar formulas, derives deterministic inner and outer programs with whole-set inference, requires a prespecified application sensitivity frontier for maintained score laws and separate arm-specific radii, and isolates terminating verified reconstruction as the genuine unresolved computational theorem.

related_work: Qiu and Stoye's equation \(2.1\) imposes Euclidean Lipschitz smoothness, equation \(2.2\) gives the tight bounded isotropic boundary-to-policy program, and equation \(2.3\) deliberately weakens it to one coordinate. Their open computational program informs the smoothness geometry but is not executed here: the direction of extrapolation and the fixed-areal observation operator are different. Piccoli and Rossi provide the flat-metric transport identity that informs the inner support-cost derivation, with Theorem 2 recording the exact special-case equivalence rather than claiming a new generic metric. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu define weighted boundary estimands and develop unit-level pre- and post-aggregation inference, which fixes the causal target but not its areal mean-information set. Mula and Nouy provide the moment-hierarchy template for value-side approximation, while Baldi and Mourrain delimit when finite exact moment extraction follows from flat truncation. Moon shows that aggregate-data sharp sets and optimization are established themes for finite-support covariates, making the continuous singular-boundary and global-Lipschitz structure essential to novelty. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer provide the general set-inversion benchmark; the present inferential claim uses exact finite-sample bounded-mean coverage and then the sharp endpoint map. Dell supplies the concrete bounded geographic-RD outcome for which a fixed-resolution sign certificate has direct substantive meaning.
technical_internal_limitation: At a boundary mean, finite multiplier attainment and exact piecewise-affine inner feasibility can fail even though the continuous primal endpoint exists. A unit-rectangle zero mean forces the true surface to vanish on the observed cell while finite dual slopes leave a positive cone value; a separate multi-cell distance-function example has a legal exposed-face mean with no exactly feasible function in any finite piecewise-affine triangulation. These are regression tests, not claimed contributions against a published estimator.
honest_scope: The population identification, transport representation, planar formulas, relative-interior approximation bounds, and confidence-box coverage are theorem targets. The terminating verified reconstruction routine is open and must pass the rational two-cell strict-interior kill test with exact continuous moments and shrinking outward gaps. Known within-cell score laws and separately selected arm-specific smoothness radii are maintained nonstandard inputs, not facts established by Qiu and Stoye or for Dell's data; the application protocol therefore reports the full prespecified sensitivity frontier and certifies a sign only when it is invariant across that grid. The sharpness claim conditions only on cell means, not on full within-cell outcome distributions. No universal boundary-face inner recovery, universal finite multipliers, floating-residual certificate, shrinking-cell asymptotic, or empirical reanalysis is claimed. When \(M_d=0\), the model reduces to constant compatible surfaces; the displayed rectangle cases recover both the vacuous interval and a strict sign interval as required sanity checks.

literature_map: Qiu and Stoye, Section 2, use equation \(2.1\) for the Euclidean Lipschitz restriction, equation \(2.2\) for the tight bounded isotropic boundary-to-policy program, and equation \(2.3\) for an explicitly one-coordinate weakening; the present fixed-areal inverse problem is informed by that setup and does not claim to execute their open program. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu define and estimate weighted boundary effects from unit-level observations; their aggregation paper's Theorems 1 and 2 and their location paper's pointwise and uniform results do not invert fixed areal means. Piccoli and Rossi, Section 3 and Theorem 13, identify the bounded-Lipschitz norm with unequal-mass transport, but have neither asymmetric clipping in the uncentered response scale nor exact side moments. Mula and Nouy's hierarchy theorem gives asymptotic value and moment convergence for semialgebraic transport, while their post-processing section recovers approximate quantities rather than exact continuous primal feasibility. Baldi and Mourrain's flat-truncation equivalence ties finite exact atomic recovery to zero-dimensional minimizer geometry, which does not cover positive-dimensional Lipschitz optimizer faces. Baldi and Mourrain's effective Putinar theorem gives quantitative pseudo-moment approximation but not the required response-surface correction. Moon's aggregate-data identified set uses finite-support covariates and polyhedral restrictions, not a continuous polygonal score, a singular boundary functional, or global Lipschitz transport. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer supply asymptotic criterion inversion for identified sets; the proposed confidence result instead starts from finite-sample bounded-mean boxes. Dell's district-level child-stunting outcome is bounded and geographically assigned, making it a concrete consumer once the known-law and smoothness inputs are defensible.

novelty_justification: Qiu and Stoye's equation \(2.1\) imposes Euclidean Lipschitz smoothness, equation \(2.2\) gives their tight bounded isotropic boundary-to-policy program, and equation \(2.3\) is an explicit one-coordinate weakening. That program informs this proposal but is not the theorem being executed: here the data reveal only finitely many area integrals and the target is a singular weighted boundary integral, so even feasibility is a different inverse problem. The closest mathematical representation is Piccoli and Rossi's Theorem 13, but exact cell moments introduce an unrestricted finite multiplier vector outside the flat-metric problem, and the response range creates deletion costs that must be derived before centering. The exact increment is therefore the integrated theorem: an attained sharp causal interval, a clipping-aware partial-transport support value, an unrestricted moment-multiplier dual with a precise relative-interior attainment frontier, explicit planar clipping laws, and finite-sample whole-set inversion. The computational frontier is stated honestly as an open-ended question: existing moment hierarchies prove convergence but do not deliver a terminating exact-moment continuous primal reconstruction and outward enclosure for every fixed strict-relative-interior mean.
